sentences.text: Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni is interpreted as a stem-ibis, an early relative of modern ibises.
The species was described by Ksepka and colleagues in 2026 based on a largely complete, articulated partial skeleton.
The specimen preserves an articulated partial skeleton, providing a rare three-dimensional view of the bird’s anatomy.
The sharply tapering tip of the beak suggests a foraging mode that involved prying mollusks from their shells.
Researchers propose that, unlike the contemporaneous R. messelensis which fed near lake margins, R. mcfaddeni may have hunted in streams.
Rhynchaeites mcfaddeni belongs to the genus Rhynchaeites, an extinct group of wading birds placed in the stem-group of the threshkiornithids.
The genus is assigned to the family Threskiornithidae and to the subfamily Rhynchaeitinae.
The type locality of the species is the Green River Formation in Wyoming, United States.
Some paleontologists question whether the parrot-like bird Mopsitta tanta should be placed within Rhynchaeites, indicating uncertainty about the genus’s broader relationships.
